domains.name: Product store
domains.promise: Members browse an owner-branded storefront via /store and the dashboard store pages, and can buy every supported product type — downloadable files with license keys, Discord perk roles and subscriptions, account-bound virtual goods, ticket-fulfilled services, and free products — through a private PayPal checkout whose fulfillment is idempotent, auditable, and strictly walled off from the play-money game economy: commerce grants only account-bound goods, never game currency, and nothing commerce grants is market-sellable.

controls.description: Master switch for the storefront: when off, /store replies that the store is closed and dashboard checkout entry points are hidden.
Which product types the owner offers; each entry unlocks its creation form on the dashboard store page and its rendering in /store.
Per-product default for what happens when a buyer who already holds an entitlement buys again: unique refuses, stackable adds another entitlement, renewable extends the term, seat-based adds a seat.
Whether a free product may be claimed once per account or repeatedly; every claim is recorded as a completed, auditable $0 order.
Allows a buyer to purchase a product for another member; the gift fulfills to the recipient through the exact same idempotent fulfillment path as a direct purchase.
When on, a completed purchase posts a celebratory message to the configured celebration channel naming only the buyer and product — never price paid by that buyer, order number, or payment details.
Discord channel id that receives public purchase celebrations; empty means celebrations stay off even if enabled.
Whether storefront and checkout surfaces derive their brand name, colors, and icon from the guild profile or from a custom owner-entered brand kit.
Maximum products rendered per /store reply page; bounded by Discord's ten-embed and five-action-row limits (one embed is the header).

defaults.rationale: The store is a headline feature and must work perfectly out of the box.
Owner decision: every product type is available immediately; owners prune rather than hunt for hidden capabilities.
Refusing accidental double-purchases by default protects buyers from surprise duplicate charges; owners opt specific products into stacking, renewal, or seats.
Owner decision: free products default to one claim per account, with repeats as explicit per-product configuration.
Gifting is part of the rich default experience and reuses the proven fulfillment path, so it is safe to enable.
Member-respectful default: purchases stay private until the owner explicitly opts into public celebration.
No channel is assumed; the owner picks one deliberately when enabling celebrations.
White-label decision: buyer surfaces carry the owner's brand from day one without configuration.
Matches the Discord embed budget: one header embed plus nine product embeds and up to five buy rows per page.

permissions.actor: Any guild member
permissions.action: Run /store, view the storefront, and start a checkout for an active buyable product
permissions.enforcement: The /store reply is ephemeral to the invoking member; the buy button re-verifies product existence, activity, and buyability server-side before any PayPal object is created.

permissions.actor: Any guild member
permissions.action: Claim a free product, producing a completed $0 order and entitlement
permissions.enforcement: Claim handler enforces the product's free-claim-policy against existing completed $0 orders for that customer before granting.

permissions.actor: Guild owner or dashboard admin with store management rights
permissions.action: Create, edit, activate, deactivate, and price products, plans, and files via the dashboard store pages and /api/store/products
permissions.enforcement: Dashboard API routes require an authenticated owner/admin session (requireGuildOwner) plus guild scoping on every products/plans/files mutation.

permissions.actor: Guild member without store management rights
permissions.action: Call product, plan, or file mutation endpoints
permissions.enforcement: Requests without an owner/admin session receive 401/403 and no row is written; Supabase RLS blocks direct table writes from non-service clients.

permissions.actor: Any actor, including the owner, through any store surface
permissions.action: Sell or grant play-money game currency, game items, or any market-sellable good through the real-money store
permissions.enforcement: Two-economies wall: product creation validation and the commerce income wall refuse currency-type or market-sellable grants; commerce-held roles earn no game role-income until their removal is proven.

messages.trigger: Member runs /store while the store is enabled and has products
messages.surface: Ephemeral Discord embed header in the /store reply
messages.defaultTemplate: Welcome to the {store-name} store! Browse below and tap Buy when something catches your eye.

messages.trigger: Buy button click passed all guards and the pending order plus grant snapshot committed
messages.surface: Ephemeral Discord embed with a PayPal link button
messages.defaultTemplate: Your checkout for {product-name} ({price} {currency}) is ready — finish up securely with PayPal below.

messages.trigger: Buyer with a live entitlement clicks Buy on a product whose repeat policy is unique
messages.defaultTemplate: You already own {product-name}! This one is one-per-person, so it stays yours alone.

messages.trigger: Member runs /store when no active products exist
messages.defaultTemplate: The store shelves are empty right now — check back soon!

messages.trigger: Products query fails while rendering /store
messages.defaultTemplate: The store could not be loaded just now. Please try again in a moment.

messages.trigger: Pending order persistence or grant-snapshot freeze failed before the payment link was exposed
messages.defaultTemplate: Checkout could not be safely recorded, so no payment link was opened — please try again.

messages.trigger: Free product claim completed
messages.surface: Ephemeral Discord embed and buyer DM receipt
messages.defaultTemplate: {product-name} is yours! Your claim was recorded as order {order-number} at no charge.

messages.trigger: Gift purchase fulfilled to the recipient
messages.defaultTemplate: Surprise! {gifter-name} just gifted you {product-name}. It is already on your account — enjoy!

messages.trigger: Purchase fulfilled while public celebration is enabled with a configured channel

messages.defaultTemplate: {buyer-name} just picked up {product-name} from the store — enjoy!

Verified payment completed; exactly one entitlement is active with roles and goods delivered and a receipt sent.
Checkout was refused or safely aborted; no payment link is live and no partial grant exists.
A storefront dependency failed; members see a friendly retry message and no state was mutated.

transitions.trigger: Member clicks the store buy button (custom id store:buy:<product-id>) from the /store reply
transitions.expectedEffect: Product identity, activity, buyability, and the buyer's existing entitlements are re-verified server-side before any money object is created.

transitions.trigger: PayPal order or subscription created, pending orders row inserted with exact identity, and commerce_freeze_order_grant_snapshot committed
transitions.expectedEffect: The payment link is exposed to the buyer only after the order row and frozen grant snapshot are durably committed.

transitions.trigger: Verified PayPal capture or subscription activation webhook for this order
transitions.expectedEffect: Exactly one entitlement is granted from the frozen snapshot via the idempotent fulfillment path; roles and account-bound goods are delivered; a receipt DM is sent.

transitions.trigger: Repeat policy refuses the purchase, the product is not buyable, or persistence failed before link exposure
transitions.expectedEffect: The buyer is told privately, any unexposed pending order is cancelled, and no PayPal link is live.

transitions.trigger: Products query or a storefront dependency fails during /store
transitions.expectedEffect: The member sees the store-unavailable message; nothing is written.

transitions.trigger: Dependency recovers and a member re-runs /store
transitions.expectedEffect: The storefront renders normally with zero residue from the failed attempt.

transitions.trigger: Buyer dismisses the refusal and browses again
transitions.expectedEffect: A fresh checkout may begin; the refused attempt left no reusable payment link or partial rows.

failures.trigger: Supabase products query returns an error during /store
failures.expectedBehavior: Reply with the store-unavailable message, write no rows, and let the next invocation retry fresh.

failures.trigger: Pending order insert fails or returns mismatched identity after the PayPal object was created
failures.expectedBehavior: Withhold the payment link entirely and tell the buyer nothing was opened; the unexposed PayPal object is never approved and no order row survives.

failures.trigger: commerce_freeze_order_grant_snapshot RPC fails or returns malformed identity
failures.expectedBehavior: Cancel the unexposed pending order and refuse the checkout so grants can never be computed from configuration that drifted after link exposure.

scenarios.promise: Out of the box, /store lists every active product with buy buttons, and buying a priced one-time product completes a private PayPal sandbox checkout that fulfills exactly one entitlement.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: A run-prefixed active product renders in /store; clicking Buy commits a pending order with a frozen grant snapshot before the payment link appears; completing sandbox payment yields one active entitlement, granted roles, and a receipt DM, all privately.

assertions.expectedObservation: /store replies ephemerally with the storefront header and product embed, the buy click returns the checkout-invite with a working PayPal link, and the buyer receives a receipt DM after capture.
Exactly one orders row (pending then completed), one payments row, and one active entitlements row exist for the purchase, guild-scoped, and no game-economy balance or inventory row changed.
audit_logs contains the checkout and entitlement.granted entries with actor, target, and product ids for the run-prefixed order.
No owner alert or DM fires for the healthy purchase; the completed order is visible in the dashboard store orders list.
Storefront and checkout embeds carry the guild-profile brand name with the powered-by-SomniBot footer; the PayPal checkout brand_name is the owner's store name, not a vendor default.
Re-clicking Buy after fulfillment is refused by the default unique policy with the already-owned message and creates no second order or entitlement.
The run-prefixed product, order, payment, entitlement, and Discord messages are removed by the sweep; audit rows remain.

scenarios.promise: Dashboard configuration takes effect: with repeat-purchase-policy set to stackable and public celebration enabled with a channel, a second purchase of the same product succeeds and a celebration posts publicly without leaking private details.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: The same buyer completes two purchases of one product yielding two entitlements, and each fulfillment posts a celebration to the configured channel naming only buyer and product.

assertions.expectedObservation: Both checkouts complete in ephemeral replies; the celebration channel shows two purchase-celebration messages containing buyer display name and product name but no order number, amount, or payment detail.
Two completed orders and two stacked entitlements exist for the buyer-product pair, and the store config row shows repeat-purchase-policy stackable and the celebration channel id.
The config change, both checkouts, and both entitlement grants each have distinct audit rows tying them to the dashboard actor and the buyer.
The dashboard admin-changes surface records the policy and celebration configuration change by the acting admin.
Celebration messages speak in the owner's configured playful voice and brand, with the subtle powered-by attribution on the embed footer.
Replaying either fulfillment webhook adds no third entitlement and no duplicate celebration message.
Both run-prefixed orders, entitlements, celebration messages, and the test config values are reverted or removed by the sweep.

scenarios.promise: A distinct configuration also takes effect: a free product under the one-claim default completes as an auditable $0 order, a second claim is refused, and a gift purchase fulfills to the recipient through the same idempotent fulfillment path.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: One completed $0 order and entitlement for the claimer with a refusal on re-claim; one gift purchase paid by the gifter that lands an entitlement and gift DM on the recipient's account.

assertions.expectedObservation: The claimer receives the free-claim-receipt with an order number, the re-claim attempt is refused ephemerally, and the recipient receives the gift-received DM naming the gifter and product.

A completed $0 order row exists for the claim, exactly one claim entitlement exists despite the second attempt, and the gift entitlement is bound to the recipient's customer row while the payment is bound to the gifter.
The $0 claim order, the refused duplicate claim, and the gift fulfillment each produce audit rows identifying claimer, gifter, and recipient.
The dashboard orders list shows the $0 order and the gift order with their sources distinguishable at a glance.
Free-claim and gift messages use the owner's brand and voice with powered-by attribution; the gift DM celebrates the gifter by display name.
Replaying the claim request or the gift fulfillment produces no second $0 order, no second entitlement, and no duplicate DM.
Run-prefixed free product, $0 orders, gift order, entitlements, and DMs are swept; audit rows for claims and gifts remain.

scenarios.promise: Invalid store configuration is rejected atomically: a product with a negative price, an unknown type, or a game-currency grant attempt never persists, and the storefront keeps serving the last valid catalog.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: POST /api/store/products with a negative price_cents, an unrecognized type, and a play-money currency grant each return a validation error; no products row, PayPal object, or partial plan is created and /store output is unchanged.

assertions.expectedObservation: /store before and after the rejected submissions renders the identical product list with no phantom or half-created product.
The products, plans, and files tables contain no rows from the rejected submissions and no orphaned PayPal catalog ids were persisted.
Each rejected mutation is recorded as a refused admin action with the validation reason, and no grant-capable row was written.
The dashboard form surfaces a precise field-level validation error to the acting admin; no alert noise is generated.
Validation error copy on the dashboard uses the product's configured voice and never exposes raw stack traces to the admin.
Submitting the same invalid payload repeatedly stays a pure no-op with identical refusals and zero accumulated rows.
Nothing to sweep beyond the valid baseline product; the sweeper confirms zero residue from the rejected submissions.

scenarios.promise: Store management is denied to non-admins: a member session cannot create, edit, or deactivate products through the dashboard API, and direct table writes are blocked by RLS.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: A non-admin authenticated session calling POST and PATCH on /api/store/products receives 403 with no row written; an anon Supabase client cannot read or write products for the guild beyond what RLS exposes.

assertions.expectedObservation: /store rendering for members is unaffected, and no member-visible surface exposes management controls.
The products table is byte-identical before and after the denied calls, and the anon client's direct insert/update attempts are rejected by RLS.
The denied management attempts are logged as permission refusals with the caller identity, and the refusal rows are never deleted.
Repeated denied management attempts from one caller surface in the dashboard security/audit view for owner review.
The 403 response body is a clean branded error envelope without internal implementation detail.
Replaying the denied requests never escalates access or accumulates partial writes.
No resources were created to sweep; the sweeper verifies the denial run left zero residue.

scenarios.promise: When PayPal is unreachable, checkout fails safe: the buyer gets a friendly retry message, no payment link is exposed, and no pending order or partial grant exists.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: With the PayPal token endpoint made unreachable, clicking Buy replies that the payment service is unavailable; the orders table gains no row, no PayPal object exists, and a later healthy attempt succeeds cleanly.

assertions.expectedObservation: The buy click replies ephemerally with the payment-service-unavailable copy and no link button; the subsequent healthy attempt shows the normal checkout-invite.
Zero orders, payments, or entitlements rows exist from the failed attempt; exactly one set exists after the recovery attempt.
The dependency failure is recorded as commerce.checkout dependency failure with the failing stage, followed by the successful checkout's normal audit trail.
Sustained PayPal unavailability raises a deduped dashboard alert for the owner rather than one alert per failed click.
The failure copy is calm, owner-voiced, and never surfaces raw provider errors to the buyer.
Hammering Buy during the outage creates no queued or deferred charges that could fire later; recovery starts from a clean slate.
Only the recovery purchase's run-prefixed rows exist to sweep, and the sweep leaves zero residue.

scenarios.promise: Transient failures converge on retry: a one-off storefront query failure recovers on the next /store, and a retried checkout after a transient refusal produces exactly one usable payment link and one order.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: An induced transient DB failure makes /store reply store-unavailable once; the immediate retry renders normally, and the buyer's retried checkout completes with exactly one pending order, one link, and one fulfillment.

assertions.expectedObservation: First /store shows the store-unavailable message, the retry shows the full storefront, and the retried buy yields one checkout-invite and one receipt.
After convergence exactly one order, one payment, and one entitlement exist; the failed attempt contributed zero rows.
The transient failure and the successful retry are both audited, letting the timeline reconstruct the recovery.
A single transient blip raises no owner alert; only sustained failure would.
Failure and success copy are both in the owner's voice, so retrying feels seamless to the member.
The retry did not resurrect the failed attempt's state; totals equal exactly one purchase.
The single purchase's run-prefixed rows and messages are swept to zero residue.

scenarios.promise: Money and grants are idempotent under replay: replaying the capture webhook, the buy click, or the free claim never duplicates an order, charge, entitlement, role grant, or receipt.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: After a completed purchase and a completed free claim, replaying the capture webhook five times and re-sending the claim request leaves row counts, role assignments, and DM counts exactly unchanged.

assertions.expectedObservation: The buyer has exactly one receipt DM and holds each granted role exactly once; no duplicate celebration or claim receipt appears.
Orders, payments, entitlements, and $0 claim rows are count-identical before and after all replays, keyed by provider ids and claim identity.
Replay attempts are visible as no-op replay audit entries without duplicating the original grant entries.
Replays raise no duplicate owner-facing order entries or alerts in the dashboard.
No replayed surface leaks internal idempotency details to the buyer; visible copy stays unchanged.
The idempotency keys (paypal order id, payment id, claim identity) provably fence every duplicate path, including gifts using the same fulfillment path.
The sweep removes the single purchase and claim footprint; replay attempts added nothing extra to sweep.

scenarios.promise: Checkout state survives a full stack restart: a pending order with its frozen grant snapshot fulfills correctly when the capture arrives after bot and dashboard restart.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: With a pending order committed and the payment link issued, the bot and dashboard are restarted; the sandbox capture webhook then fulfills exactly one entitlement from the frozen snapshot, and /store works immediately after boot.

assertions.expectedObservation: After restart the buyer's receipt DM arrives and granted roles appear, and /store renders the storefront on first invocation.
The pending order row and grant snapshot are unchanged across restart and transition to completed exactly once.
The audit trail spans the restart seamlessly: checkout before, fulfillment after, with no gap or duplicate.
No spurious owner alerts fire from the restart itself; the order shows completed in the dashboard.
Post-restart surfaces render identical owner branding with no fallback to defaults.
Any webhook redelivered around the restart window is absorbed idempotently with no double grant.
Run-prefixed rows created before the restart are fully swept after it, proving cleanup does not depend on in-memory state.

scenarios.promise: Concurrent buyers are safe: two simultaneous buy clicks on a unique-policy product, or two simultaneous free claims under one-claim, yield exactly one grant and one clean refusal.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Two parallel buy interactions for the same buyer and unique product resolve to at most one fulfillable order and one entitlement; two parallel claims on a one-claim free product resolve to one $0 order and one refusal.

assertions.expectedObservation: One interaction proceeds to checkout or claim success while the other receives the already-owned refusal; neither hangs or double-replies.
At most one entitlement and one completed $0 order exist per race despite concurrent inserts, enforced by database-level uniqueness rather than bot memory.
Both racing attempts are audited with their outcomes, and the winning grant appears exactly once.
The dashboard shows a single order per race with no phantom duplicate pending rows left behind.
The losing racer's refusal copy is the friendly branded already-owned message, not an error dump.
Late-arriving duplicate fulfillments from the losing attempt are fenced by the same idempotency keys.
The sweep removes the single grant footprint and any cancelled loser order rows, verifying zero residue.

scenarios.promise: Guild isolation is absolute: a second guild never sees the first guild's products, orders, or entitlements, and purchases in one guild mutate only that guild's rows.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: With products created in guild A only, /store in guild B shows the store-empty message; a purchase completed in guild A adds zero rows scoped to guild B, and guild B's dashboard store pages stay empty.

assertions.expectedObservation: /store in guild B replies store-empty while guild A renders its catalog; no cross-guild product or receipt leaks into guild B channels or DMs about guild B.
All run rows carry guild A's id; queries scoped to guild B return zero store rows, and RLS prevents guild B admins from reading guild A commerce data.
Audit rows for the run are exclusively guild A scoped; guild B's audit view is empty of store events.
Guild B's owner receives no alerts, orders, or DMs from guild A activity.
Each guild's storefront shows its own brand configuration, proving branding is guild-scoped too.
Replaying guild A's fulfillment webhook cannot be redirected to grant anything in guild B; the custom id's guild binding is enforced.
Sweeping guild A leaves guild B untouched, and both guilds finish with zero run residue.

scenarios.promise: The suite cleans up after itself: every run-prefixed store resource — products, plans, orders, payments, entitlements, roles, and Discord messages — is removed, while audit history is preserved.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: After the domain's scenarios, the cleanup pass deletes or reverts all run-prefixed resources in Discord, Supabase, and PayPal sandbox catalog objects, and a final verification query set returns zero residue while audit rows remain intact.

assertions.expectedObservation: Run-created store messages, celebration posts, and granted test roles are gone from the guild after the sweep.
Zero run-prefixed rows remain in products, plans, orders, payments, entitlements, or customers created solely for the run.
Audit rows from the run remain append-only and undeleted, with personal fields anonymized where the retention contract requires.
The owner surface shows no lingering test orders or alerts after the sweep.
Any branding configuration changed during scenarios is restored to its pre-run values.
Running the cleanup pass twice is idempotent: the second pass deletes nothing and errors on nothing.
The final sweep report enumerates every created resource id and confirms its removal or intentional audit retention.

domains.name: PayPal payments
domains.promise: PayPal is the money rail: every webhook is signature-verified against the configured webhook id before processing, every capture, subscription event, and refund is processed exactly once with replay-exact effects, refunds are provider-first with an append-only attempt ledger that never guesses an ambiguous provider outcome, and legacy USD-mislabeled sale rows remain refundable under an explicit tolerance.

controls.description: Order of operations for owner-initiated refunds: provider-first confirms the PayPal refund outcome before local entitlement and payment state flip; local-first is not offered for money paths.
Maximum signature verification attempts per delivery (one initial call plus quick retries) before the route answers 503 so PayPal redelivers.
Age after which a webhook event stuck in processing (for example from a crash) may be reclaimed and resumed by a new delivery.
Accepts refund events against historical subscription sale payments whose currency label was persisted as a hardcoded USD, matching on exact evidence before tolerating the label mismatch.
Which PayPal API base the stack talks to; the proof suite always runs against sandbox and live is an explicit owner cutover.
Days a subscription entitlement stays in grace_period after a failed payment before automatic revocation, giving PayPal dunning time to recover the charge.

defaults.rationale: Owner decision: never flip local money state until PayPal has confirmed the refund, so the ledger can never claim money moved that did not.
Matches the shipped verification budget: one call plus two quick retries fits inside the webhook time budget while riding out API blips.
Five minutes matches the shipped stale-processing constant: long enough for slow handlers, short enough that crashed events resume on the next redelivery.
Historical sale rows were persisted with a hardcoded USD label; refusing their refunds would strand real customer money, so the tolerance ships on with exact-evidence matching.
Every automated proof runs against PayPal sandbox; switching to live is a deliberate owner action, never a default.
Matches the shipped suspension default: three days of retained access covers typical PayPal payment retry cycles without extending free access indefinitely.

permissions.actor: PayPal delivering to POST /api/paypal/webhook with headers that verify against the configured webhook id
permissions.action: Have the event processed into orders, payments, entitlements, and bot fulfillment actions
permissions.enforcement: verify-webhook-signature is called with the transmission headers before any handler runs; only a SUCCESS verification proceeds.

permissions.actor: Any caller whose webhook signature fails verification
permissions.action: Trigger any processing, row write, or fulfillment
permissions.enforcement: Failed verification returns 400 with zero side effects; verification-service unavailability returns 503 so PayPal redelivers instead of processing unverified.

permissions.actor: Guild owner authenticated on the dashboard
permissions.action: Drive a refund for an order via POST /api/orders/[id]/refund
permissions.enforcement: requireGuildOwner gates the route; each attempt is admin-rate-limited and recorded in the append-only refund attempt ledger with a stable request id.

permissions.actor: Any member, admin without owner rights, or unauthenticated caller
permissions.action: Call the refund endpoint
permissions.enforcement: The route returns 401/403 before touching the ledger; no PayPal call is made and no attempt row is created.

messages.trigger: Payment capture or first subscription payment completed and fulfillment succeeded
messages.defaultTemplate: Thanks for your purchase! Order {order-number}: {product-name} — {amount} {currency}. Your access is live.

messages.trigger: Subscription payment failed and the entitlement entered grace_period
messages.defaultTemplate: A payment for {product-name} did not go through. You keep full access until {grace-ends} while PayPal retries — nothing to do if it recovers.

messages.trigger: PayPal confirmed a refund as COMPLETED and local effects were applied
messages.surface: Buyer DM and dashboard order detail
messages.defaultTemplate: Your refund for order {order-number} ({amount} {currency}) has been completed by PayPal.

messages.trigger: A refund attempt reached PayPal but the outcome is not yet definitive
messages.defaultTemplate: Refund attempt {attempt-id} for order {order-number} is awaiting a definitive PayPal outcome; the ledger holds it as pending and will finalize on the next poll.

messages.trigger: Webhook signature verification service is unavailable after all retry attempts
messages.surface: Dashboard alerts panel and owner DM
messages.defaultTemplate: PayPal webhook signature verification is failing ({reason}). Deliveries are answered 503 so PayPal redelivers them — no event has been lost or processed unverified.

messages.trigger: A webhook delivery failed signature verification
messages.defaultTemplate: A webhook delivery failed signature verification and was rejected without processing (transmission {transmission-id}).

messages.trigger: A refund webhook arrived before its originating capture or sale event
messages.defaultTemplate: A refund event for payment {payment-id} arrived before its payment record; it fails resumably and PayPal redelivery will process it once the payment row exists.

values.description: Webhook endpoint healthy and idle; no delivery in flight.
A delivery arrived and its signature is being verified against the configured webhook id within the attempt budget.
Verified event claimed for processing under its provider event id; handlers apply exactly-once effects.
The event's full effect set (rows, entitlements, queued bot fulfillment) is durably committed and recorded against the event id.
Processing failed for a resumable event type; the exact snapshot will resume on PayPal redelivery without duplicating effects.
A non-resumable event exhausted redelivery; the owner replays it deliberately from the dashboard webhook log.
An owner refund attempt is in the append-only ledger awaiting a definitive provider outcome.
PayPal confirmed the refund; the payment row, entitlement revocation, and buyer notice are applied exactly once.

transitions.trigger: PayPal POSTs a delivery with transmission headers to /api/paypal/webhook
transitions.expectedEffect: Verification runs before any body-derived effect; unverified content cannot touch the database.

transitions.trigger: Signature verification returns SUCCESS within the attempt budget
transitions.expectedEffect: The event row is claimed under its provider event id so concurrent duplicates observe the claim.

transitions.trigger: The event handler commits its full effect set
transitions.expectedEffect: Payments, entitlement transitions, license issuance, and queued bot actions exist exactly once, keyed to the provider ids.

transitions.trigger: A handler for a resumable event type throws after partial progress
transitions.expectedEffect: The staged snapshot is preserved; result is recorded as resumable failure so redelivery resumes rather than restarts.

transitions.trigger: PayPal redelivers the same event id
transitions.expectedEffect: The resumed run completes the remaining effects without duplicating totals, license keys, or queued actions.

transitions.trigger: A non-resumable event type fails
transitions.expectedEffect: The event is parked with full payload for deliberate owner replay from the dashboard; nothing partial leaks to buyers.

transitions.trigger: Owner submits a refund for a captured order
transitions.expectedEffect: A new append-only attempt row is written with a stable provider request id before any PayPal call.

transitions.trigger: PayPal reports the refund COMPLETED (directly or via poll/webhook)
transitions.expectedEffect: Payment status flips, the entitlement is revoked through the exact revocation RPC, and the buyer is notified — each exactly once.

failures.trigger: The PayPal verification API is unreachable or times out for every attempt in the budget
failures.expectedBehavior: Answer 503 so PayPal redelivers, raise a deduped owner alert, and process nothing unverified.

failures.trigger: A delivery's transmission signature fails verification
failures.expectedBehavior: Reject with 400, write zero commerce rows, and record the rejection in the security log.

failures.trigger: A refund request to PayPal times out or returns an indeterminate status
failures.expectedBehavior: Hold the ledger attempt as pending, never write a second create for the same request id, and finalize by polling the provider until the outcome is definitive.

failures.trigger: A refund webhook arrives before its capture or sale event created the payment row
failures.expectedBehavior: Fail the event resumably so PayPal redelivery re-processes it once the payment row exists; never fabricate a payment to refund.

domains.name: License keys
domains.promise: License keys are secure by construction and self-serviceable: keys are stored only as hashes (SMNI-prefixed, shown in full exactly once at issuance), activation via /license activate binds strictly to the purchasing Discord account, compromised keys are rotated — never revealed — and buyers manage their own device sessions within the configured device limit through the portal and license SDK endpoints.

controls.description: Keys are persisted as SHA-256 hashes with only prefix and suffix retained for display; the full key exists in plaintext only in the one-time issuance message.
What happens when a buyer asks to recover a key: rotate-and-invalidate issues a fresh key and kills the old one immediately; reveal-existing is never offered because plaintext keys are not stored.
Per-product default for how many concurrent device sessions one license key may hold before new activations are refused until a slot is freed.
Lets the key holder sign out individual devices from the portal (and via /api/license/deactivate on uninstall) without contacting the owner.
Expected interval between SDK heartbeats; sessions missing heartbeats beyond a multiple of this interval stop counting toward the device limit.
Brand prefix on generated keys (format PREFIX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX); part of the product's white-label surface.

defaults.rationale: Hashed-only storage means a database leak cannot leak usable keys; this is a hard security default.
Owner decision: recovery is rotation, never reveal — the old key dies instantly and the new one is shown once.
Three devices covers a desktop, laptop, and spare for a single honest buyer while keeping sharing visible to fraud detection.
Portal self-service decision: buyers free their own device slots without support round-trips.
Hourly heartbeats keep session liveness fresh without burdening client apps or the API.
Matches the shipped generator's SMNI-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX format; owners may rebrand the prefix per product.

permissions.actor: The Discord account the key was issued to (bound_discord_id)
